messages.subject_clean: Error: ncol(X) == ncol(con.mat) is not TRUE
messages.body_plain:
Hi again Chris;

I see you updated the package which is very good but also has a learning curve for me. This time my question is very simple;

After creating graph list "g" as you instructed on user guide, I created contrast matrix for simple group comparison with

con.mat <- matrix(c(0, -2), nrow=1, dimnames=list('Control > Patient'))

I created data table X with Study.ID and Group variables with

X <- covars[, 1:2]

Then when i try summary function with brainGraph_GLM, dummy coding

summary(brainGraph_GLM(g, measure='E.nodal.wt', covars=covars[, 1:2], + coding='dummy', con.mat=con.mat, alt='greater'))

I get this error;

Error: ncol(X) == ncol(con.mat) is not TRUE

But ncols(X)=2 and ncols(con.mat)=2

This is a very simple design, what am i doing wrong?   :/

I am using brainGraph ver 2.20 from GitHub

Best wishes
Ozgun

messages.body_plain:
It's possibly an error when using "covars[, 1:2]" to create the design matrix. Is "covars" a "data.table" object?
When you choose "coding='dummy'", this adds a column for the Intercept term; if the first 2 columns of "covars" are, for example, "Study.ID" and "Group", then I don't know what is causing the error. But if the "Group" column has data type "factor", and there are more than 2 levels in the factor, this could be causing the error. Please let me know the following:

1. What does "covars" look like?
2. What does the output of: brainGraph_GLM_design(covars[, 1:2], coding='dummy') look like, as well?

Chris

g.glm <- c(g[[1]][[5]], g[[2]][[5]])

messages.body_plain:
Hi Jaiashre,

1. As Ma & Mondragon (2015) write, there isn't a consensus method for defining the vertices that make up the rich club. So their *rich core* method determines the rich club members without regard to a random graph model or statistical significance. To answer your question, there also isn't a consensus for choosing a cut-off value when considering multiple groups at once. You may decide on the minimum of the group-specific values, or the maximum, or some other number (the plotting function automatically shades in starting at the maximum across groups). Choosing where there is "separation" is too arbitrary, I would think.

2. It is possible that there is statistical significance for both groups; but the asterisks *might* be plotted on top of one another. This would be a bug in the plotting function (I have to double-check). To see the values, you can access the data by something like:
plot_rich_norm(rich.dt, ...)$data

i.e., by accessing the "data" element of the function's return object.

3. Normalized rich-club coefficients that are > 1 are considered to indicate the presence of rich-club ordering in the network. But the value isn't necessarily significant, this requires comparison to a set of random graphs. I don't think you can compare normalized rich-club coefficients between groups (e.g., 1.1 vs. 1.5). The values are only meaningful relative to the set of random graphs, and therefore the topology of the observed network.

4. Sure, if you use "rich_core" you can do something like:

core <- rich_core(g)
vertex_attr_dt(g)[degree > core$k.r]

If you otherwise create "rich.dt" (following the User Guide), you can just do:
rich.dt[p < .05]

Or change to "p.fdr", or change the ".05" to ".01", etc.

Chris

Here is the code I used to plot that figure:

plot_brainGraph_multi(g, groups=1:2, N=N,filename='Figure02_richClub_revision.png',
  subgraph=list(paste('degree >=', rich_core(g[[1]][[N]])$k.r),
                       paste('degree >=', rich_core(g[[2]][[N]])$k.r)),
  vertex.color='color.lobe', edge.color='color.lobe', vertex.size='degree',
  vertex.label=NA, sub=NULL, cex.main=4)

As you can see, I used "rich_core" to decide which vertices to include (via the "subgraph") argument.

If you would like to change the edge attribute "size.rich", you would have to do something like the following (this is actually the code from the function "rich_club_attrs"):
E(g)[E(g)$type.rich == 'rich-club']$size.rich <- 3.5
E(g)[E(g)$type.rich == 'feeder']$size.rich <- 1.5
E(g)[E(g)$type.rich == 'local']$size.rich <- 0.5

For the *vertex* attribute "size.rich", here is from the same function:
V(g)[V(g)$rich == 1]$size.rich <- vec.transform(V(g)[which(V(g)$rich == 1)]$degree, 3, 15

What "vec.transform" does is it takes a numeric input vector (in this case, the degree sequence of the rich-club vertices), and "transforms" it so that it fits into a range of 3 to 15. So change these values to something else, or simply do something like:

V(g)[V(g)$rich == 1]$size.rich <- 10
V(g)[V(g)$rich == 0]$size.rich <- 1

or whatever you like.

Chris

messages.body_plain:
Hi Jaiashre, unfortunately since you're doing a structural covariance network analysis, you cannot get modularity for each subject. The graphs that are stored in list element "g[[1]]" are all of those for Group 1, where "g[[1]][[1]]" is *Group 1, threshold/density 1*; "g[[1]][[2]]" is *Group 1, threshold/density 2*; and so on.

So, there is no subject-level data to access. Each gray matter region would have to be the same size for that to be possible, but as you know Freesurfer regions are not all equal sizes.

You mention you want the mean and standard deviation for power analysis. For the mean, you can use the observed value; i.e., "g[[1]][[1]]$mod" for example. For the standard deviation, you must do bootstrapping. See Chapter 13.1 of the User Guide for more information on this.

Chris

messages.body_plain:
Hello, I have just updated the package to v2.3.0. As usual, you can find the NEWS.md file on the Github page: https://github.com/cwatson/brainGraph

This update consisted mostly of bugfixes:

* `mtpc`: fixed bug when calculating statistics for different values of "alternative"

* bootstrapping: fixed bug when calculating *weighted* global efficiency; new argument "xfm.type" to handle this; it is the same behavior as for `set_brainGraph_attr`

* `plot.brainGraph`: you now do not need to specify a value for "hemi" if you select "plane='sagittal'"; it will by default select "hemi='L'"

* `plot_rich_norm` had a few bugs, and now has a new argument "smooth". This only works with single-subject networks, and plots a smoother instead of a line for every subject's rich-club curve.

A new feature is that `set_brainGraph_attr` now calculates, at the graph-level, *weighted characteristic path length*; this is simply the mean of the vertex-level values.

Finally, if your *Study.ID* variable is integer/numeric, the functions in the package will convert to character to avoid any errors.

As usual, please let me know if there are issues. I will update the User Guide today or tomorrow (although there is not much to update).
Chris

Please make sure you are using 2.3.2 instead of 2.3.0 or 2.3.1. I apologize for any issues these bugs have caused.
